turns.reply: I checked what the platform can actually see for this objective. Card Expiry is a real, filterable attribute on the Card entity, so the 'week before expiry' timing is buildable as an audience entry. 'Actively transacting' would need Transaction-entity attributes (type, status, amount, initiated-by) — these exist too, but are marked new/not-confirmed-built, and more importantly the builder only lets one entity's conditions drive a single audience entry or event entry. It cannot combine 'Card.Expiry is in 7 days' AND 'Transaction history shows recent activity' in one filter. That means the audience you actually get depends heavily on how you want these two conditions traded off, which I cannot decide for you. I also don't yet know what you'd call success, which the brief says is unsettled, and I don't know what action you actually want the customer to take before the card lapses (renew/activate a replacement, re-point auto-debits, or just not be surprised) — each of those points to a different goal event and a different message. None of these can be inferred from what's already been said, so I'm asking before designing anything.
questions: How will you judge whether this campaign worked — e.g. fewer cards going inactive after expiry, replacement cards activated, reduced service complaints, something else? If you don't have a target yet, that's fine to say.

What should count as 'actively transacting' (e.g. at least one transaction in the last 30/60/90 days, or a spend/frequency threshold)? And since the builder can filter the entry audience by the card's expiry date OR by transaction records, but not both together in one condition set, which should define who enters the campaign: expiry-date timing (and we note activity as an unenforced assumption), or an activity filter (and we lose the precise 'week before expiry' timing)?

What do you want the customer to actually DO before the card expires — request or activate a replacement card, update auto-debit/standing instructions to the new card, confirm their address for physical delivery, or just be informed so payments aren't disrupted? This decides the goal event and the call to action.

turns.reply: Your reply confirms the priority between the two entry signals — expiry timing first, activity second — and that settles one structural fork: the campaign will enter customers off Card Expiry (the week-before window), since the builder can't combine a Card-entity filter and a Transaction-entity filter in one entry condition set. I'm treating activity as a secondary, non-enforced signal rather than a hard filter, and I'll flag that trade-off explicitly in the proposal rather than quietly dropping it. That resolves the structural half of the earlier activity/timing question; the exact 'how many days of activity counts as active' threshold no longer forks the design (since it won't be a hard entry filter), so I'll default it and move on. Two things your reply still doesn't touch, and both would send this campaign in genuinely different directions: (1) what you'll count as this campaign working, and (2) what you actually want the customer to do before the card expires. Without (2) I don't know whether the goal event is a replacement-card activation, an auto-debit update, an address confirmation, or just 'was informed' — these point to different goal events, different CTAs, and in one case no provable goal at all. Without (1) I don't know what the business is actually trying to move, separate from the goal event itself.

turns.reply: The objective 'more customers using the card for online spend' is broad enough to support genuinely different campaigns depending on who is targeted and why they are not spending online today. I checked what events, attributes and channels the platform actually exposes: there is no direct 'online transaction' flag, but Transaction events carry Transaction Type, Transaction Status, MCC and Initiated By (MCC could plausibly separate e-commerce MCCs from others, though the value list is free-form and unverified). Card Activated / Card Issued events also exist (marked new/proposed) which would suit an activation-moment campaign. Before I pick between these I need to know who you mean and what you believe is blocking them, because that decides the entry event, the audience, and the message itself — and I still need your definition of success, which this brief says is not yet settled.
questions: Who is the primary target: customers who have never used this card online at all (activation), or customers who already spend online occasionally but you want spending more often or at higher value (growth)? These lead to different audiences and a different entry point.

What's your own read on why these customers aren't using the card online more — e.g. they haven't set it up / verified it for online transactions, they default to a different card for online purchases, they don't know they can, or something else? This shapes what the message needs to overcome.

How do you want success judged here — e.g. number of distinct customers who complete at least one online transaction in a given window, growth in total online spend, repeat online usage, or something else? This is yours to define; I'll track whatever you decide.

turns.reply: Your reply confirms you have no data and no hypothesis on why customers favour offline spend — I'm treating that as a real answer: we won't assume a specific blocker and will design a message that works whether the issue is awareness, habit, or friction, rather than guessing one cause. Two other questions remain unanswered and I want to separate them from the data point, because they're not about data at all — they're decisions only you can make, and each one leads to a genuinely different campaign. I also want to flag something the tooling just confirmed: there is no 'online vs in-store' flag anywhere on a Transaction event (not in Transaction Type, Transaction Status, or Initiated By). MCC exists but is free-form and unverified for this tenant, so I cannot confirm any MCC list would reliably mean 'online purchase' here. This affects how precisely either campaign can actually detect 'online spend' as a goal, and I'll carry it into the proposal as a limitation either way — it doesn't change which of the two questions below I still need from you.
questions: Who should this reach first: customers who have NEVER made an online purchase with this card (getting them to try it once), or customers who already spend online sometimes but you want spending more often or in higher amounts (growth)? This isn't about data you have — it's which group you want to prioritise. These lead to different audiences, different entry points, and different messages, so I can't guess it.

How do YOU want success judged — e.g. number of distinct customers who make at least one online transaction in a set window, growth in online transaction count per customer, or growth in online spend value? This is your definition to give, not something derivable from data.

questions.text: Who is the primary target: customers who have never used this card online at all (activation), or customers who already spend online occasionally but you want spending more often or at higher value (growth)? These lead to different audiences and a different entry point.

What's your own read on why these customers aren't using the card online more — e.g. they haven't set it up / verified it for online transactions, they default to a different card for online purchases, they don't know they can, or something else? This shapes what the message needs to overcome.

How do you want success judged here — e.g. number of distinct customers who complete at least one online transaction in a given window, growth in total online spend, repeat online usage, or something else? This is yours to define; I'll track whatever you decide.

Who should this reach first: customers who have NEVER made an online purchase with this card (getting them to try it once), or customers who already spend online sometimes but you want spending more often or in higher amounts (growth)? This isn't about data you have — it's which group you want to prioritise. These lead to different audiences, different entry points, and different messages, so I can't guess it.

How do YOU want success judged — e.g. number of distinct customers who make at least one online transaction in a set window, growth in online transaction count per customer, or growth in online spend value? This is your definition to give, not something derivable from data.

answers.text: I do not have any data on this. I do not know why they use it offline more, and we have no numbers on it.

facts.statement: I do not have any data on this. I do not know why they use it offline more, and we have no numbers on it.

limitations: Stated as unavailable by the user: I do not have any data on this. I do not know why they use it offline more, and we have no numbers on it.

dimensions.name: target segment (activation vs growth)
dimensions.rationale: Determines audience, entry event, and the core intervention — activation customers need a first-use nudge, growth customers need a frequency/value nudge. These are different campaigns, not variants of one.

dimensions.name: perceived blocker to online spend
dimensions.rationale: Would have shaped the message's core argument (setup friction vs awareness vs habit vs trust).
dimensions.note: User stated twice, across two rounds, that no data or hypothesis exists on why customers favour offline spend. Deferring: the message will be written to address the most plausible generic blockers (awareness that the card works online, and low visible friction) rather than targeting one unconfirmed cause.

dimensions.name: success definition
dimensions.rationale: Determines what goal event and measurement the campaign is built and read against; this is the business's own yardstick, not something to infer.

dimensions.name: moment/trigger for intervention
dimensions.rationale: Depends directly on the segment answer above — activation implies entering near card issuance/activation, growth implies entering on a cadence or after low online-spend evidence. Will resolve once segment is answered.
